short: ZFX and its Y-linked paralogue ZFY are thirteen-finger C2H2 zinc-finger activators that bind a short GC-rich site containing a GGCCT core. Their placement is the interesting part: they bind inside CpG-island promoters a couple of hundred base pairs downstream of the transcription start site, between the open region at the TSS and the first downstream nucleosome, and they activate the promoters they occupy. Together with the related ZNF711, they occupy the majority of active CpG-island promoters in a cell. ZFX loss slows proliferation, which is why the gene recurs in growth-based CRISPR screens, and ZFX supports embryonic and hematopoietic stem-cell self-renewal. Germline ZFX variants cause an X-linked neurodevelopmental disorder.
long:
## The factors

ZFY was cloned in 1987 from the sex-determining region of the human Y chromosome and proposed as the
testis-determining factor [PMID:3690661], a role later taken by SRY [PMID:1695712]. Its X-linked paralogue ZFX has a similar gene
structure, escapes X inactivation [PMID:2500252], and was recognized early as a probable transcriptional activator
with alternative isoforms [PMID:2512506]. The third member, ZNF711, is also X-linked and has an overlapping binding
pattern [PMID:32406922]. All three are ubiquitously expressed, which is unusual among C2H2 factors and consistent
with a housekeeping role at promoters.

The proteins have an acidic N-terminal region and thirteen C2H2 zinc fingers. Mutational dissection
shows that fingers 11 to 13 are necessary and sufficient for DNA binding, and that these fingers
together with the N-terminal region constitute a functional transactivator [PMID:32406922]; the remaining ten fingers
are not required for site recognition. In the databases behind this family, only ZFX has matrices,
and the four of them agree closely (cohesion 0.91), so this is one of the more internally consistent
zinc-finger families despite the short motif.

## The motif

The consensus is GC-rich and short. The core that all models share is GGCCT, and the fuller form used
by JASPAR and CIS-BP is GCCBMGGCCT, which is also the data consensus for this family; the HOCOMOCO
ChIP-derived version, CCAGGCCBCG, is the same core with different flanks. There is no crystal or NMR
structure of the ZFX fingers on DNA, so which bases the three DNA-binding fingers contact is inferred
from the standard C2H2 recognition rules rather than observed. With roughly five to eight informative
positions, the motif is one of the least specific in routine use, and it is intrinsically GC-rich, so
matches are dense wherever GC content is high. Reported analyses note that the GGCCT motif occurs
throughout the genome but at higher density inside CpG islands, which is where occupancy is found [PMID:29429977].

ZFX, ZFY and ZNF711 are not separable by sequence in practice, and their genomic binding patterns at
CpG-island promoters are essentially the same. ZNF711 also has its own reported motif, and where the
two are distinguished, ZFX appears to be the dominant of the pair, with ZNF711 playing a subordinate
role at shared promoters [PMID:32406922].

## Where it acts

This family is a promoter family, and the position of binding is its defining feature. ChIP in four
cancer cell lines recovered roughly 9,000 ZFX sites, most of them in CpG-island promoters, and genes
with ZFX-bound promoters were expressed at higher levels than unbound ones [PMID:29429977]; knocking ZFX down
down-regulated many of them, so ZFX is an activator. The binding position is about 240 base pairs
downstream of the transcription start site of responsive promoters, and nucleosome-occupancy and
methylome sequencing places it between the nucleosome-free region at the TSS and the first downstream
nucleosome [PMID:29429977]. Taking ZFX, ZFY and ZNF711 together, the union of their bound promoters covers on the
order of 10,000 CpG-island promoters, a large majority of the active CpG-island promoters in a cell [PMID:32406922].
Mechanistically, reducing ZFX lowers histone H4 acetylation and increases RNA polymerase II pausing
at target promoters [PMID:38726870], which is consistent with a role in promoter architecture and early elongation
rather than in enhancer-driven, cell-type-specific regulation.

## Biology and disease

Zfx-null mice are viable but smaller, with reduced self-renewal of embryonic and hematopoietic stem
cells [PMID:17448993], so the gene supports proliferative capacity rather than specifying a lineage. That fits the
cancer literature, in which ZFX expression correlates with proliferation and outcome across several
tumor types, and in which Zfx facilitates tumorigenesis driven by Hedgehog-pathway activation [PMID:25164012].
Because ZFX contributes to growth in many cell types, bi-allelic ZFX knockouts reduce cell growth and
combined ZFX/ZNF711 knockouts cause major proliferation defects [PMID:32406922], which is why ZFX turns up repeatedly
as a hit in growth-based genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens; readers should be aware that a ZFX hit
in such a screen usually reflects this general proliferative requirement rather than a
pathway-specific dependency. In human genetics, germline ZFX variants cause an X-linked
neurodevelopmental disorder with a recurrent facial gestalt [PMID:38325380]. ZFY, on the Y chromosome, has a distinct
role in male germ-cell development [PMID:37354519].

## Reading a hit

A GGCCT-containing match is weak evidence by itself: the motif is short, GC-rich, and denser in CpG
islands, so hits accumulate in exactly the sequence people usually submit. Position is the most useful
filter. A match a couple of hundred base pairs downstream of a CpG-island TSS is a plausible ZFX site;
the same match in an intergenic or AT-poor enhancer is probably not. The hit identifies the family
rather than the protein: ZFX, ZFY and ZNF711 bind the same sequence, and which one matters depends on
the sex and expression of the cells. Note also that the CIS-BP human ZFX motif in this collection is
transferred from mouse Zfx rather than measured on the human protein, though at 99% DNA-binding-domain
identity that transfer is harmless. Finally, because ZFX sits at a large fraction of all active
promoters, a ZFX-like motif recovered from another factor's ChIP data is more likely to reflect
promoter co-occupancy than that factor's own specificity.
caveats: The motif is short (roughly five to eight informative positions) and GC-rich, so hits are dense in CpG islands and GC-rich sequence generally, and a match alone means very little. Position carries more information than score: credible sites lie a couple of hundred base pairs downstream of a CpG-island transcription start site. ZFX, ZFY and ZNF711 read the same sequence and cannot be separated, and only ZFX has matrices here; the CIS-BP entry is transferred from mouse Zfx, benign at 99% DNA-binding-domain identity. No structure of these fingers on DNA exists, so the base contacts are inferred. Because ZFX occupies most active CpG-island promoters, a ZFX-like motif in another factor's ChIP data usually means co-occupancy.

timeline.finding: A zinc-finger gene, ZFY, is cloned from the sex-determining region of the human Y chromosome and proposed as the testis-determining factor.
timeline.methods: Deletion mapping of the Y chromosome in sex-reversed individuals, cDNA cloning
timeline.open: No DNA-binding site was known, and the assignment rested on map position.

timeline.finding: The X-linked paralogue ZFX is shown to have the same gene structure, to escape X inactivation, and to encode alternative isoforms with the features of a transcriptional activator, making the pair a dosage-related gene family rather than a male-specific switch.
timeline.methods: Genomic and cDNA comparison, X-inactivation escape assays, domain analysis

timeline.finding: SRY is identified as the testis-determining factor, removing the role that had motivated interest in ZFY and leaving the family without an assigned function for a decade.
timeline.methods: Positional cloning in sex-reversed individuals, sequence analysis

timeline.finding: Zfx-null mice are viable but small, with reduced self-renewal of embryonic and hematopoietic stem cells, giving the family a proliferative rather than a lineage-specifying role.
timeline.methods: Conditional mouse knockout with stem-cell transplantation and self-renewal assays

timeline.finding: ChIP in human tumor cell lines places roughly 9,000 ZFX sites overwhelmingly in CpG-island promoters, about 240 base pairs downstream of the start site, between the nucleosome-free region and the first downstream nucleosome, and knockdown lowers expression of bound genes, so ZFX is an activator positioned by promoter architecture rather than by enhancer context.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq in four cell lines, knockdown with RNA-seq, nucleosome-occupancy and methylome sequencing
timeline.open: Whether ZFY and ZNF711 occupy the same promoters was untested.

timeline.finding: Treating ZFX, ZFY and ZNF711 as one family shows their bound promoters cover on the order of 10,000 CpG islands, that zinc fingers 11-13 are necessary and sufficient for DNA binding, and that losing ZFX and ZNF711 together causes major proliferation defects.
timeline.methods: CRISPR bi-allelic knockouts in HEK293T, RNA-seq, structure-function analysis of ZFX mutants

timeline.finding: Reducing ZFX lowers histone H4 acetylation and increases RNA polymerase II pausing at target promoters, which recasts the family as acting on promoter chromatin and early elongation rather than on recruitment of the polymerase.
timeline.methods: Degron and knockdown of ZFX with chromatin profiling and nascent transcription assays

timeline.finding: Germline ZFX variants are shown to cause an X-linked neurodevelopmental disorder with a recurrent facial gestalt, establishing that a factor sitting at most active CpG-island promoters is dosage-sensitive in human development.
timeline.methods: Clinical exome and genome sequencing in a patient cohort with functional assays

open: How ZFX is positioned a couple of hundred base pairs downstream of the start site is unexplained: the GGCCT core is short and common in CpG islands, so either an unidentified feature of promoter architecture selects the bound copy, or the position reflects nucleosome placement rather than sequence.

Whether ZFX, ZFY and ZNF711 differ at all in intrinsic specificity is untested; their measured motifs are the same and their promoter occupancy overlaps, so the apparent dominance of ZFX over ZNF711 at shared promoters has no sequence explanation.

No structure of the ZFX fingers on DNA has been determined, so which bases fingers 11-13 contact is inferred from the standard C2H2 recognition rules rather than observed, and the GCCBMGGCCT and CCAGGCCBCG forms in the databases have not been reconciled structurally.
Whether the transcriptional effects of ZFX loss are direct or follow from a general proliferation defect is hard to separate, which is also why ZFX recurs as a hit in growth-based CRISPR screens.
